topics.name: Prepositions of place: in, on, between, under

options: There are hundreds of star in the sky.
There are hundred of stars in the sky.
There are hundreds of stars in the sky.
questions.rule: hundreds of is followed by a plural noun: hundreds of stars.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct preposition.
options: The birds fly on the sky.
The birds fly in the sky.
The birds fly of the sky.
questions.rule: Birds, clouds and stars are in the sky.

options: A butterfly is on the lawn.
A butterfly are on the lawn.
A butterfly am on the lawn.
questions.rule: One thing takes is: a butterfly is.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: These and are show more than one, so the noun is plural: lambs.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Hundreds of stars is plural, so use are.
two needs a plural noun. Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: butterflies.
a bird is one thing, so: There is a bird.
Plural lambs goes with are.

chat: What did you see at the beach?
options: I see lots of shells yesterday.
questions.rule: lots of + a countable noun takes the plural: lots of shells; past question, so saw.

chat: Is there any milk in the fridge?
questions.rule: milk cannot be counted and takes a singular verb: there is some milk.

options: The childrens are feeding the lambs.
The children are feeding the lambs.
The child are feeding the lambs.
questions.rule: child becomes children in the plural (no -s added).

options: How many shells did you collect?
How much shells did you collect?
How many shell did you collect?
questions.rule: We can count shells, so ask How many + plural noun.

options: There is a dewdrop on every leaf.
There are a dewdrop on every leaf.
There is dewdrops on every leaf.
questions.rule: One thing: There is a dewdrop. Many things: There are dewdrops.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: sand cannot be counted, so use much: too much sand.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Something resting on top of a thing is on it: sitting on the flowers.
Stars can be counted, so use How many.
Inside water or a space, use in: in the pond.
Plural five bees takes There are.

chat: How many bees did you see?
options: I saw much bees near the flowers.
I saw many bee near the flowers.
I saw many bees near the flowers.
questions.rule: many goes with a plural countable noun: many bees.

options: It is on the table, Mom.
questions.rule: A thing resting on a surface is on it, and it takes is.

options: Two sheeps and three lambs are in the field.
Two sheep and three lamb are in the field.
Two sheep and three lambs are in the field.
questions.rule: sheep stays the same in the plural; lamb becomes lambs.

options: There is not many water in the pond.
There are not much water in the pond.
There is not much water in the pond.
questions.rule: water cannot be counted: use much and the singular verb is.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: all my needs a plural noun. The plural of tooth is teeth.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: many shells is plural, so: There are many shells.
goose has an irregular plural: one goose, three geese.

questions.after: not any clouds in the sky today.
questions.rule: clouds is plural, so: There are not any clouds.
milk cannot be counted, so ask How much milk is left?
under tells us the place below something: under my bed.

chat: Name some animals that live on a farm.
questions.rule: Irregular plurals: sheep stays sheep, ox becomes oxen (no extra -s).

options: Yes, there is two mangoes left.
Yes, there are two mango left.
Yes, there are two mangoes left.
questions.rule: two mangoes is plural: there are two mangoes.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence about yesterday that is correct.
options: Hundreds of shells were lying on the shore yesterday.
Hundreds of shells was lying on the shore yesterday.
Hundreds of shell were lying on the shore yesterday.
questions.rule: Plural shells takes were in the past.

options: There were many bees in the garden last summer.
There was many bees in the garden last summer.
There were much bees in the garden last summer.
questions.rule: Past + plural: There were; countable bees take many.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Last night is past and hundreds of stars is plural, so: there were.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: sugar cannot be counted, so use much: so much sugar.

questions.after: time, so we ran to the bus stop.
questions.rule: time here cannot be counted, so use much.

questions.after: me and my brother at dinner.
questions.rule: Use between for two people or things (me and my brother); among is for more than two.
children is plural, so the past form is were singing.
To ask, put the verb first: Are there any birds ...? (plural birds)

chat: What did you do on Mother's Day?
options: I make a card and baked two cakes for her.
I made a card and baked two cakes for her.
I made a card and baked two cake for her.
questions.rule: two needs the plural cakes, and both verbs are past: made, baked.

chat: Is there much traffic on the road?
options: Yes, there are too many cars on the road.
Yes, there is too many cars on the road.
Yes, there are too much cars on the road.
questions.rule: Countable plural cars: there are too many cars.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct prepositions.
options: My mother's photo hangs on the wall between the two windows.
My mother's photo hangs in the wall between the two windows.
My mother's photo hangs on the wall among the two windows.
questions.rule: Pictures hang on a wall; for two things use between.

options: How much loaves of bread and how many milk do we need?
How many loafs of bread and how much milk do we need?
How many loaves of bread and how much milk do we need?
questions.rule: many + countable (loaves; loaf becomes loaves), much + uncountable (milk).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: With exactly two things, use between, not among.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: women is the plural of woman, so the verb is plural: have started.

questions.after: on the lawn were wet with dew.
questions.rule: All the ... were needs a plural. leaf becomes leaves (f changes to -ves).

questions.after: a few clouds, but today the sky is clear.
questions.rule: Yesterday is past and a few clouds is plural, so: there were.
Countable plural: How many dewdrops are ...?
all her is followed by the plural children; one mother takes loves.

chat: Where should I keep the flower vase?
options: Keep it among the two lamps on the shelf.
Keep it between the two lamps on the shelf.
Keep it between the two lamp on the shelf.
questions.rule: between is for two things, and two needs the plural lamps.

chat: Why are you up so early?
options: There was hundreds of birds singing outside my window.
There were hundreds of bird singing outside my window.
There were hundreds of birds singing outside my window.
questions.rule: Plural hundreds of birds takes were, and hundreds of needs a plural noun.
